metadata.title: Why One Always-Present Token Secretly Hijacks Every Attention Statistic
metadata.purpose: When no key is strongly preferred, softmax must still spend its probability somewhere; the ever-present, semantically-neutral BOS token becomes the low-resistance sink where heads park leftover attention — so any max-reduction that includes it reports the sink, not the structure.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the attention heatmap: column 0 glowing in every row, planted with the raw 91%/verb-subject stat; returns masked, diverse real patterns light up)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes that when one token wins the attention max almost every time, it must be the real signal. It isn't — it's the sink. So: signal, or sink?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Token zero keeps winning the attention max — that must be the real signal, right?', hesitates on 'signal', corrects to 'sink'

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Single-word trigger ('signal') swapped for a single-word replacement ('sink') so buildActs()'s whitespace-token match fires. TIMING LAW: 28-word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('signal' -> 'sink') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Look at one real attention head: layer four, head three, across fifty thousand sentences. Token zero — the sentence-start marker — wins the max-attention position in ninety-one percent of them, with more than half the weight every time. The verb-to-subject link everyone expects only shows up once token zero is excluded from that count.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - a heatmap grid, column 0 glowing terracotta across every row

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - the attention heatmap
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A grid of cells, rows = sentences, columns = token positions (BOS, The, cat, sat, on, the, mat). Column 0 fills terracotta and glows across every row; the remaining columns hold faint, varied ink tints. Stat callout beneath: '91% of rows, weight > 0.55'. THIS EXACT GRID COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess: if one position wins that statistic almost every time, across thousands of unrelated sentences, it must be carrying the sentence's real meaning — attention is supposed to point at what matters most.

shot.new_visual_element: Column 0 spotlighted, arrows converging on it from many sentence icons, labeled 'the real signal?'

production_viz.label: The natural guess - it must be the signal
production_viz.mechanic: A single highlighted TOKEN 0 card in the center. Several small sentence-icon rectangles surround it, each with a thin arrow converging on the card, suggesting every sentence's meaning routes through this one position. Label beneath: 'the real signal?'

beats.narration_text: But softmax has to spend all of its probability on every single row, whether any position deserves it or not. Token zero is present in every sequence and carries no sentence-specific meaning, so it's the cheapest place to park the leftover weight — that's not a discovery about meaning, it's just where the math had nowhere else to go.

shot.new_visual_element: 'the real signal?' struck through; a probability bar forced to sum to 1, leftover mass draining into the always-present empty seat

production_viz.label: The break - it's the cheapest seat, not the signal
production_viz.mechanic: The B02 TOKEN 0 card and its converging arrows fade to low opacity (no line crosses the label glyphs). Beneath it, a horizontal probability bar spanning the full width, labeled 'must sum to 1'; most segments are thin and unclaimed, and the mass drains into one wide terracotta segment on the far left labeled 'always present, no meaning — cheapest seat'.

beats.narration_text: Take one sentence starting with that marker: the raw weights might read something like point five eight on the marker and far less on every real word. Run that pattern across a thousand sequences and the marker wins the max ninety-four percent of the time. Exclude just that one position from the count, and the real dependency — the verb pointing back to its subject — wins sixty-eight percent instead.

shot.new_visual_element: small bar chart of raw weights (marker vs. real words); before/after stat 94% raw max -> 68% once excluded

production_viz.label: The worked example - raw weights, then excluded
production_viz.mechanic: Four short bars labeled BOS / The / cat / sat with values 0.58 / 0.04 / 0.12 / 0.09, BOS bar tall and terracotta, the rest short and ink-tinted. Beside it, two stat cards appear in sequence: 'raw max: 94%' then, after BOS is struck, 'excluded: sat -> cat wins 68%'.

beats.narration_text: One direction: seeing the sink dominate a head's max doesn't mean that head learned nothing. The real signal can still be sitting in the rest of the row — it's just outweighed by the one reflex position the moment you only look at the max.

shot.new_visual_element: a row's full distribution: tall sink bar, smaller real bars still present, labeled 'still there, not the max'

production_viz.label: The sink doesn't erase the rest of the row
production_viz.mechanic: One full row of small bars: a tall terracotta bar on the left (the sink) beside several shorter ink bars of varying height to its right, none struck or faded. Label beneath the shorter bars: 'still there, not the max'.

beats.narration_text: The other direction: a head that doesn't lean on token zero isn't automatically trustworthy either — it might just be parking its leftover weight on a different filler, like a comma or a padding token. Mask out the known non-signal positions across this same head, and the patterns that were invisible before — real subject, object, and verb links — light up across almost every row.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - same heatmap, column 0 masked out, diverse real patterns lighting up across the remaining columns

production_viz.label: The anchor returns - masked, the real patterns light up
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 HEATMAP GRID RETURNS, identical layout. Column 0 fades to a flat gray 'MASKED' column. Across the remaining columns, cells that were faint now brighten into varied, structured patterns (diagonal bands suggesting subject/verb/object links) row by row.

beats.narration_text: One always-present, meaning-empty token quietly wins nearly every attention statistic you compute — exclude it before you trust what the rest of the pattern is actually showing you.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I'm looking at attention weights in a transformer, and one position — often token zero — keeps winning the max across almost every head and layer. Walk me through how to check whether that's a real signal or an attention sink, and show me how to redo the statistic with that position excluded so I can see what's actually underneath it. Liam, in for Bear.
